**Likely yes, but not yet corroborated under the tool’s rule.** The data show 13.5 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2025, or 3.91% of the asset. Of that area, 13.1 hectares were mapped as native forest in Uruguay’s 2021 forest map, and 98% was mapped as forest by the JRC in 2020.

The finding remains provisional: the series ends in 2025, so no later year was available to corroborate the event. Tree-cover loss alone also does not establish the cause or whether the forest was permanently converted.
